title: DefenseCon 2956 Ship Q&A | Star Citizen
summary: Q&A DefenseCon New Ships There's a full payload of new ships dropping this DefenseCon, and we know you want that sweet, sweet intel.
body_html:
Q&A DefenseCon New Ships There's a full payload of new ships dropping this DefenseCon, and we know you want that sweet, sweet intel.

We hit up the Vehicle and Gameplay teams to fire off the hard-hitting questions about every ship blasting onto the scene at DefenseCon 2956. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.

DRAKE IRONCLAD & IRONCLAD ASSAULT How have the Ironclad and Ironclad Assault evolved since they were first concepted, and how have other recent flyable ships informed their development? Since their concept, the primary change to both Ironclads has been the internal layout in the rear half of the ship, prioritizing ease of traversal throughout what is a complex environment. The original concept interior had a lot of back-and-forth traversal across the width of the ship. Now, there are additional stairwells and ladders to help cut down movement time.

Other changes occurred in the hold, which resulted in increased cargo capacity by adjusting the cargo grid size to allow for more space utilization while maintaining a clear path through the center.

Both the Ironclad and Ironclad Assault appear to be well equipped for multiple roles beyond their intended use as armored freight and combined-arms platform respectively. What types of multi-crew gameplay do you see them excelling at? Both platforms have the capacity to go well beyond their intended roles simply due to their cargo areas’ sheer size and volume. For example, other vehicles can be stowed within the cargo hold, allowing the Ironclads to serve as motherships or hubs for other gameplay loops.

With the release of the Ironclad, the Caterpillar will also receive its Command Module. While the Ironclad’s module can be used with the Caterpillar, is the reverse also true, and how does the module differ from the original Caterpillar concept? Both ships now share an identical Command Module. When making the current Command Module, we wanted to ensure the role of the previous one was maintained for Caterpillar owners, hence why it still has the beds and drop seats. So, regardless of which ship it’s attached to, it can function as the “life raft” as originally intended.

Can you tell us more about the Ironclad Assault’s fabricator? What can it craft, and how does it fit into the ship's broader utility role? Like the Clipper, the Ironclad Assault features a fabricator, and when available in a future patch, it will be able to craft any available blueprint directly to and from the cargo grid. However, it is not enabled at launch due to the functionality of fabricating to and from vehicle grids not currently being available.

The Ironclad includes multiple tractor beams. Are they all the same, or do they differ in functionality? They are all the same size but, due to their locations and ability to be moved (much like the RSI Hermes’ tractor rail), they provide multiple angles of coverage for loading and unloading.

How does the Ironclad Assault’s repair and refuel functionality work, and can it be used on small ships as well as ground vehicles? Like other select ships in Alpha 4.8, the Ironclad Assault features the initial implementation of Ship Hangar Services. This is currently ship-wide, so any ground vehicle or ship within the Ironclad Assault can utilize it. However, in a future patch, this will be limited to the rear third of the cargo bay, which is the designated repair area.

It was previously mentioned that the Ironclad could not be flown independently with the Command Module detached, although the main hull would still retain some core functions such as power, cooling, tractor-beam control, and self-defense. How do you envision pilots making use of these capabilities in-game when the command module is detached? The ability to leave behind the main hull allows for easier atmospheric entry and exit while leaving the parent ship above the planet to carry on doing whatever activities are required.

How will insurance claims work when the command module is detached and the main ship is lost or destroyed? If the main ship is lost or destroyed, the claim will return the host vehicle with a new Command Module attached, effectively claiming both at once. Any previously stored Command Module from that ship will be bricked, whether it was stored at the time of the claim or not. Bricked modules remain visible in the Fleet Manager and can be removed from the ASOP through the new scrap option.

If the loadout is insured, players can select the insured loadout option when filing the claim. This returns both the Command Module and the host vehicle with a snapshot of the prior loadout changes applied.

The Command Module can also be claimed on its own, without triggering a claim on the host vehicle.

With ship armor now implemented, how does this system affect the Ironclad and Ironclad Assault's performance and role in the broader fleet, and how do they sit within the landscape of ships like the M2, C2, and Starlancer series? With armor now active, the Ironclad takes its place as a durable industrial hauler, plated for sustained industrial operations. The Ironclad Assault carries improved armor on top of that, letting it endure stressful situations better than the civilian variant.

Looking at armor capabilities, the Ironclads sit in the middle of the pack, better protected than lighter civilian haulers, like the C2 Hercules and Starlancer, but below more refined military platforms, like the M2 Hercules. Even so, both Ironclad variants carry more base hull HP, letting them keep soaking up damage long after lighter rivals would be disabled, extending their operative time in hostile space.

DRAKE PITBULL Can you give us an overview of the Pitbull’s armaments and what kind of targets it was built to take on? In classic Drake form, the Pitbull has more guns than comparable craft, providing plenty of firepower at the expense of durability.

The Pitbull joins a competitive snub fighter category alongside ships like the Mirai Fury. What sets it apart? The Pitbull trades resilience for aggression. Where the Fury concentrates its fire through 4× S2 guns, the Pitbull spreads it across 6 barrels (4× S1 plus 2× S2), putting more rounds on target at the cost of per-shot punch. Built on a lighter frame, it pitches harder, accelerates faster, and turns tighter in the close fight but pays for that edge with a more fragile hull that cannot trade hits.

How many Pitbulls can the Ironclad Assault carry, and what does that open up for groups running them together? Simply put, lots. With some careful arrangement, it can easily be into double figures, allowing for the Ironclad to become a snub carrier.

With Tactical Strike Groups releasing alongside the Pitbull, how does the ship's hit-and-run design philosophy translate into that gameplay? While not packing heavy firepower to damage larger ships, a swarm of Pitbulls is a great hit-and-run deterrent to help screen larger ships and provide complementary fire support.

In addition to dogfighting and swarm tactics, the Pitbull’s minimalist approach and high speed seem like they’d make for a competent racer. Is this something the team considered during production? Naturally, given their size and relative agility, most snubs suit racing, but the Pitbull is not specifically tailored to it.

As a snub fighter lacking a quantum drive, the Pitbull was clearly designed to be carried within a larger vessel. Which ships was the Pitbull designed to fit within? Part of the initial brief criteria for the Pitbull was to not exceed the volume of the Fury to maximize transport suitability, so any ship that can fit a Fury should be capable of fitting a Pitbull. A great thematic example is the Drake Ironclad Assault, as this allows both the storage of multiple Pitbulls as well as Ship Hangar Services, providing fleet support to other operations, such as mining or escort.

DISCLAIMER These answers accurately reflect development's intentions at the time of writing, but the company and development team reserve the right to adapt, improve, or change feature and ship designs in response to feedback, playtesting, design revisions, or other considerations to improve balance or the quality of the game overall.

Referral Bonus FAQ Find everything you need to know about the DefenseCon 2956 referral bonus. Referral Bonus FAQFind everything you need to know about the DefenseCon 2956 referral bonus. What is the referral bonus? The referral bonus gives you free gear for getting new players into Star Citizen. This time, you will receive a Drake Dragonfly with Coalfire paint when you refer a friend. The player you refer will receive a DefenseCon Gear Pack, including matching hat, T-shirt, and cargo pants.

The bonus is granted when a new player uses your referral code and pledges for a starter pack or ship (minimum ) on the Pledge Store.

The usual referral bonuses apply too, including 50,000 aUEC and a point in the regular Referral Program.

This bonus promotion runs until May 27, 2026, 20:00 UTC.

How do I refer a friend? Your friends should add your personal referral code when creating their new RSI accounts. Once an account is created, a new player has 24-hours to add a referral code to their account to claim their rewards if they did not add it at account creation. More info on this process can be found here.

Where do I find my personal referral code? You can find it on the Referral Program Page. Your Referral Code is unique and can be shared anywhere you like, including on social media, via email, or on your website.

What’s in it for me? Recruiting one friend during the promotion gets you a Drake Dragonfly, a rugged snub for adventurers looking to live on the edge. Dual-mode conversion allows the Dragonfly to operate on the ground or in space, and a rear-facing second seat means you can even take a passenger! This reward also includes the Coalfire paint.

What's in it for them? The player you refer during the promotion can walk into DefenseCon ready to represent after receiving a DefenseCon Gear Pack, including matching hat, T-shirt, and cargo pants. They can make a statement and rep the brand that's got the fans' back...on their actual back.

Can I earn more than one Drake Dragonfly? No. Only one Drake Dragonfly with Coalfire paint can be earned per player.

What is the regular Referral Program? The regular Referral Program empowers you to become a driving force behind the growth of the Star Citizen community. Plus, you’ll unlock cool in-game rewards, from exclusive hangar items to ships. The Referral Program Page details everything currently available.

When do I receive my referral bonus? The veteran player will receive their bonus immediately when the new player they are referring pledges for a starter pack or ship (minimum ) on the Pledge Store. The new player's bonus will be granted once the promotion ends on May 27. Bonuses may be distributed in waves, so if you don't see it show up right away, it should populate soon.

Are there any limitations to the referral bonus? Yes. The Drake Dragonfly with Coalfire paint given out as a referral bonus includes LTI (Lifetime Insurance) and is non-meltable and non-giftable.

Do the standard Referral Program and the limited DefenseCon 2956 Referral Bonus work together? Yes. All referrals gained during the bonus period go towards your total in the standard Referral Program.

Where can I find more information on the Referral Program? Click here to check out our regular referral program.

Click here to find the Referral Program FAQ.

title: Life, Death, and Life Again Beyond 4.3.1
summary: Introduction Medical Gameplay, like other systems within the Star Citizen universe such as mining and salvage, is not a standalone endeavor within the overall development of the project. It is inexorably and essentially linked with several other systems like the Actor Status System, Scanning, FPS traversal, beacons and more.
body_html:
Introduction Medical Gameplay, like other systems within the Star Citizen universe such as mining and salvage, is not a standalone endeavor within the overall development of the project. It is inexorably and essentially linked with several other systems like the Actor Status System, Scanning, FPS traversal, beacons and more.

Because of this, forward development is often dependent on outstanding work to related-systems first, and it can often seem like this vital and important aspect of our intended Star Citizen experience has taken a back seat to other, flashier systems.

This unfortunate reality was compounded earlier this year with the release of Server Meshing, which had an adverse effect on beacons, which were not and still have not been fully updated and converted to the multiple star system reality of 600 players we have today.

While Alpha 4.3.1 brings several new aspects to medical beds and restores some of the recently lost rescue beacons functionality, we wanted to take this opportunity to explore the intended future for regeneration beyond Alpha 4.3.1.

This is not the comprehensive Death of a Spaceman we're still driving towards, but a brief exploration of some of the changes and additions we'll encounter along the way, all currently in development.

It is also worth noting that similar to every other Design Brief we've done, the information within accurately reflects our current development intentions at the time of publishing, but we always reserve the right to listen, adapt, improve, or change features and designs in response to feedback, playtesting, design revisions, or other considerations to improve balance or the quality of the game overall.

Life, and Death, and Life Again Beyond 4.3.1

While much of medical gameplay is rightly aimed at preventing death, we must still do everything we can to prepare for the worst, while giving you meaningful and strategic options for getting back into the 'verse as soon as possible post-death.

To that end, the following additional changes to medical beds are currently in development:

Adding the ability to imprint on multiple medical beds at once.

Adding the ability to choose which imprinted medical bed you wish to regenerate at.

Adding new conditions which may limit regeneration, such as cooldown timers or regeneration limits before re-registration of an imprint is required.

Multiple Imprints at Once

The first key to this will be to allow you to have multiple imprints at different locations simultaneously, allowing you a tactical choice upon incapacitation if no help is available, of choosing where you regenerate next.

These choices will fall into one of four categories:

MedBed Conditions

In Alpha 4.3.1 the MedGel requirement was added to medical beds, providing another condition that needed to be met for successful healing and regeneration: being stocked.

In the future, there may be other conditions you encounter that affect or limit your ability to use a specific medical bed either owned by another player or found in the wild. These are not global conditions applied to all medical beds, but specific states enabled by deliberate content or player action.

Additionally, some of these conditions may be found combined with one another.

Medbed Permissions If a medical bed is within your ship, vehicle or base, then you may set permissions limiting who can use it to heal and imprint independently:

Only You (overrules all other options)

Everyone (overrules options below)

Friends

Party Members

Org Members

Changes to the Regeneration Interface

To account for these changes, including the ability to imprint and regenerate at multiple locations and apply a variety of status conditions to a medical bed, a new interface is currently in development.

Rescue Beacons

Since the launch of Alpha 4.0 the Rescue Beacon system has suffered from several legacy design elements that are waiting to be updated:

With the increased player capacity of 600 people, the existing notification system became unmanageable and needs to be refactored.

With the addition of multiple star systems, the marker system needs to be updated to provide intermediate destinations (like a nearby jump point.)

With both factors, a better way of finding and sorting them is needed.

Additionally, we need several UI improvements, including a way for first responders to see the last several medical beacons a player has sent, to better judge the likelihood of ambush.

While we can provide no dates or estimates for when these fixes and additions will arrive, we wanted to acknowledge that we're aware of the issues, and re-iterate our intention to address these issues on our road to 1.0.

A Note to the First Responders

Of the many aspects that excite us about this universe we continue to build each and every release, medical gameplay, and specifically the role of first responders in the 'verse, is something that inspires many of us to continue bringing these facets to life.

Whereas mining, salvage, transport, racing, combat and more all provide personal dividends in credits/loot/bragging rights, the acts of those who dedicate their time specifically, intentionally and frequently towards helping others has a nobility and positive effect on everyone. These are acts we want to better support going forward.

This begins with the medical bed evolutions listed above, and continues through restoring and improving the rescue beacon system in the future, but there's even more we can do on our journey towards Death of a Spaceman and Star Citizen 1.0. It will take time, and we'll share more details as those releases approach, but in the meantime, we wanted to say that we see you: those people who fight not for riches and individual prosperity, but to help your fellow citizen day in and day out, and make the persistent universe a better place to live in.

Thank you for helping others, and we're exploring what more we can do to help you along the way.

title: Re: Ironclad/assault
summary: Ciao! The expected damage behaviour when the Command Module is docked to the Ironclad/Caterpillar is as follows: Armour: The Command Module inherits all armour values of the ship to which it is docked. Damage Propagation: When bullets strike the Command Module while docked, the damage is transferred directly to the host ship. This damage remains with the host ship and is not transferred to the Command Module upon undocking. Shields: When docked, the Command Module is covered by the host ship's shields and utilises only the host ship's shield items, never its own. If any of these behaviours are not respected, you may have encountered a bug. In that case, we would appreciate it if you could contribute to an existing Issue Council report or create a new one if needed.  Thanks! Montic - Vehicle Experience Team

title: Alpha 4.8: Vehicle Insurance and Item Bricking Update
summary: Hi everyone,   With the release of Alpha 4.8, we’re introducing several updates to vehicle insurance along with a new item bricking system. Read on for a full overview of what’s changing and what to expect.     High-Level Overview  The current claim system has served us well, but as the universe becomes more persistent (and eventually dynamic), we want vehicle loss and recovery to feel more meaningful. At the same time, you shouldn't feel like the game is working against you when you just want to get back out there.   The updates coming in Alpha 4.8 are designed to strike that balance: adding more depth and consequence to insurance and item recovery, while supporting the long-term vision for Star Citizen’s living economy and persistent universe.     Insured Loadouts  Going forward, your ship will have two distinct loadouts.   The manufacturer loadout is the default configuration of your ship. It cannot be edited and will always be there as your fallback.   The insured loadout is yours. It's the custom configuration you built and want to protect. You can still edit through the Vehicle Loadout Manager in your mobiGlas, but to save your loadout, you’ll need to head to an ASOP terminal. When you save, you'll see a full list of every item being registered under that loadout before you confirm.    In future updates, insured loadouts will also cover items in weapon racks, suit lockers and decorations.   At the launch of Alpha 4.8, any items attached to your ship that you do not imprint will be lost and unrecoverable. Due to a feature limitation, this temporarily includes any vehicle-equipable items or paints acquired through the pledge store, or attributed via the RSI website. We intend to address this next week with a patch update enabling the ability to recover any lost pledge items for vehicles you may have forgotten to imprint, via the freight elevator. This will be followed with a more robust item kiosk offering in July’s 4.9.     Claim Timers & Insurance Claims  We’ve reworked the claim timer system to make recovering your ship feel more natural within a persistent universe, while also reducing downtime in many common situations.   Instead of the timer only starting once you file a claim, it now begins running in the background as soon as your ship is delivered to your hangar. In practice, that means some or even all of the wait may already be completed by the time you actually need to make a claim. The system keeps progressing while you play.   As part of this update, claim expedites have been removed.   When filing a claim, you’ll now choose between two recovery options:   Manufacturer Claim  Longer wait time   No UEC cost   Returns the default manufacturer loadout   Does not restock missiles or bombs    Insured Claim  Shorter wait time   UEC cost based on your ship hull and insured components   Returns your saved custom loadout   Does not restock missiles or bombs    To help support these changes, we’ve also increased payouts for select missions and reduced the cost of vehicle consumables.     Item Bricking  We’re introducing item bricking in Alpha 4.8 as part of our ongoing efforts to address item duplication.   Any item registered as part of your manufacturer or insured loadout is tied to that vehicle. When you file a claim, any previous copies of that ship and its registered components will begin a bricking countdown.   During that countdown, everything will continue functioning normally. Once the timer expires, those items become bricked and can no longer be used.   For 4.8, bricked items and vehicles cannot be sold to shops or dismantled for parts. We’ll continue iterating on this system in future updates.   One important note: bricked vehicles will remain stored in your hangar rather than being removed automatically. This gives you time to recover any cargo or personal items before the vehicle is permanently retired.     Vehicle Storage Adjustments  Local hangars now have a storage limit. Once you hit the cap, you'll need to scrap ships to free up space. Any ship you own that gets scrapped can always be claimed back through your ship catalogue, so nothing is permanently lost.   ---  As always, we’ll be closely monitoring the backend data and keeping a close eye on your feedback.   Have questions? Let us know below and we'll do our best to get answers from the team.

title: Tactical Strike Groups - FAQ
summary: "Tactical Strike Group" is our new cooperative ship combat experience, available in Alpha 4.8: "Tactical Strike"! A series of coordinated objectives awaits your team, where every ship and every pilot has a job to do. Bring the right ships, the right weaponry, and a proper plan to keep your pilots repaired and resupplied, from capital ships down to your boots-on-the-ground FPS players. Note that a strong reputation (Rank III+) with Intersec is required to access the mission.  Intersec is looking to you to assemble a small and well-balanced group of citizens to protect the People's Alliance ship Tranquility and their captured pilot from hostile Shattered Blade forces.  Here's what you need to know before you launch. ▲ What are Tactical Strike Groups? A Tactical Strike Group is an Operation, a cooperative mission chain that challenges a group of players to work together across multiple roles: dogfighting, torpedo/missile attacks, FPS combat, logistics, and more.  Success depends on bringing the right mix of ships, loadouts, and the means to keep your team repaired and resupplied on the field throughout the mission in the new location, a QV Extraction Station.  The mission can be shared with other players in your party.   ▲ How do I find a QV Extraction Station? Open your mobiGlas and accept one of the following Mercenary Contracts from Deacon Tobin, Intersec’s contract giver, which will lead you to the QV Extraction Station: :clipboard: Tactical Strike Group Needed - Full multiplayer mission. Bring a large party. :boom: Strategic Attacks - Solo mission focused on surface-to-ground attack ships. :fire: Assist People's Alliance Vessel Tranquility - Solo dogfighting mission for fighter pilots.   ▲ Can I replay this content? Yes, absolutely, Tactical Strike Group missions are fully replayable, allowing you to increase your reputation and earn more rewards!   ▲ What roles does my group need to cover? Plan for around 10 ships and skilled pilots crewing these, and covering these core roles: :sparkles: Dogfighting - Skilled fighters will be needed to repel enemies. :boom: Surface attacks - Torpedoes, missiles, strafing runs... Prepare the proper armament to destroy heavy turrets and key defenses protecting the station. :zap:️ Tight-space maneuvering at higher speeds - Trench run anyone? That's your job: get rid of defenses and station's components to protect your party and give breathing room for your landing troops. :fire: FPS Combat - You'll need a ground team to complete FPS objectives inside the station, and of course a Dropship to land them safely! :beginner: Logistics - Rearm, resupply, heal, and support your pilots. :package: Hauling - Prepare enough cargo grid to move your loot from the station to your favorite stash.   ▲ What rewards can I look forward to? Completing the mission can yield blueprints, flight suits and helmets, high-quality ship components, a unique bomber jacket, rare trade commodities, and of course some good ol' aUEC for your trouble!   ▲ Mission Walkthrough (Spoilers) :one: Defend the Idris An Idris, owned by People's Alliance and piloted by Captain Aniss Martell, is under attack from the Shattered Blade ships beneath the station, out of sight of the Vanduul tech turrets. Work together to eliminate all threats before moving on with your next objectives.  :two: Destroy the power relays Navigate the turret-defended exterior and destroy 6 power relays to open the station's maintenance tunnels. Note that relays are only vulnerable to ballistic damage, so energy weapons won't cut it.  :three: Destroy the cooling units Fighter ships must navigate distortion-filled internal tunnels in multiple runs to destroy 18 cooling units. As units fall, the core overheats (glowing brighter, emitting smoke) until the shield doors and exterior vents open automatically.  :four: Destroy the core and defend the People's Alliance's Idris With the core exposed, destroy 4 internal core stabilizers or attack the core directly from the exterior (It requires significantly more damage, however). Once the core is gone, all Vanduul and security turrets go offline. Simultaneously, the People's Alliance Idris will call for help again under a harder wave of Shattered Blade attackers. Split your forces or concentrate firepower, your call to adapt to the situation at hand.  :five: FPS: free the hostage Deploy your ground team to the now-unlocked landing pad. Fight through Shattered Blade Elites and their boss "Forge" to reach the security room, then use the terminal to open the hangar doors for the People's Alliance hostage ship. The hostage will tip you off about a security card left behind, and hint that one of two cargo decks is locked and worth investigating.  :six: Escort the hostage "Gabe Windell" to safety Protect the People's Alliance hostage ship as it spools up to quantum travel. Vanduul reinforcements arrive in force! If the People's Alliance Idris is still combat-ready, it will assist your team to help in combat against a greater Vanduul foe: a Mauler! Hold on long enough for the hostage to Quantum away: This is your win condition. Of course, don’t forget to loot the station’s rooms and anything you spotted during the operation. Salvage what you can, bring it back, and share the spoils with your party!   ▲ Any last tips? Coordination is everything. Designate roles before you undock: Assign a team to pilot and manage your carrier. Have a logistics team ready to repair/replace/resupply your fighters. Hire expert torpedo boats and missile gunships. Get a solid FPS team and enough supplies to last while in the station. Prepare a fully loaded support ship, keeping your forces repaired and rearmed. You might not succeed at first, but learn from your mistakes and come back fully prepared!   :avocado: Tips from the Evocati A ship capable of rearming and repairing fighters is crucial during TSG. The Idris series, Polaris, and Ironclad Assault currently excel in that role, but ships like the 890 Jump, 600i, Carrack, or Starlancer TAC can also get the job done. - MrTrash Bring an engineer on board to handle fires, repair components, and even provide support fire with a railgun! - Evens Don’t forget your best ally, the People’s Alliance Idris. You can use it to repair, rearm, and refuel when needed. - Le_Roux-nard The Sabre Firebird and Talon Shrike are excellent options for surface attack roles. - Ewentx Avoid staying too long in the tunnels during trench runs. It’s better to make multiple passes than risk getting disabled by distortion building up inside the station. - Farden For trench runs, consider a Size 2+ power plant and running as a duo, so the pilot can focus on maneuvering while the gunner handles the objectives. - Samm Gelfond Medics, remind your party memebers to set their regeneration in your main ship! - Tsuya_Arcanys Communicate with your ally to avoid crashing into each other in the station's tunnels - Narmacil

title: Join DefenseCon 2956
summary: Hi everyone,  Get ready, DefenseCon returns bigger & better from May 14 through May 27.  When the UEE pulled Invictus back to Sol, DefenseCon didn’t wait for orders, Drake Interplanetary CEO Anden Arden has seized the moment to throw the galaxy's boldest arms expo in their place. Whether you're a seasoned pilot looking for your next weapon of choice or just someone who believes every citizen deserves the right ship, DefenseCon 2956 has one message for the galaxy: the Navy can keep its formalities, we'll keep the explosions.  Join the celebration at the Bevic Convention Center in Area18, where manufacturers will showcase their fleets and offer free test flights of some of the most iconic and formidable military ships in the ’verse: Throughout the event, you’ll have ongoing opportunities to pilot a diverse selection of cutting-edge spacecraft, all available in one place. Also, be sure to stop by the IO-North Tower as well, where you can take in the sight of the massive Anvil Odin battlecruiser, perfectly positioned for a breathtaking view over Area18.  But there’s more than just ships to fly, as DefenseCon comes with a full lineup of events and festivities. Everyone can take to the skies during the Free Fly event, an exclusive Referral Bonus rewards those who bring new recruits into the 'verse, and Twitch Drops opportunities will be enabled! Enjoy everything DefenseCon 2956 has to offer: DefenseCon 2956 || FAQ Manufacturer Schedule - For the first time ever, Drake takes the helm as it brings all ship manufacturers together for its biggest event ever! Tobii's Everyday Heroes Screenshot Contest - Be a hero and show it to the world, for a chance to earn some of the new ships coming this DefenseCon, including two Tobii Eye Tracker 5! Drake Ironclad and Ironclad Assault || Q&A Drake Pitbull || Q&A Origin M80 || Q&A MISC Starlite || Q&A Aegis Tiburon || Q&A Anvil Odin, concept || Star Citizen Live - DefenseCon Showcase: Odin Battlecruiser Play for FREE during Drake DefenseCon 2956 - The Free Fly will run through May 27. ⁠Referrals - Refer a friend and get your Drake Dragonfly + Coalfire paint! Your recruit will receive a DefenseCon T-Shirt, hat, and cargo pants. Twitch Drops - Head to Twitch/StarCitizen, and tune in to any Drops enabled stream for a total of four hours to unlock the Tailwind ‘Murray Cup’ flight suit and helmet, for free. New Player Guide Welcome Hub, for new players || Welcome Back, for returning pilots

title: Tobii's Everyday Heroes Screenshot Contest
summary: Forget the Navy's polished ceremonies. Drake built DefenseCon 2956 for one reason: to celebrate the people the UEE forgot. The haulers, the medics, the everyday heroes holding the 'verse together. The real ones. No rank required. Just show up.  We want to celebrate those hardworking folks who keep it all humming. Did you answer a beacon and revive a downed Citizen in need? Had a friendly hauler come to your rescue when you were stranded on a distant moon? Or maybe you showed a new pilot the ropes and helped load their cargo. If a player did anything cool that made someone else's day, that counts!  Whatever it is, if it made a difference, no matter how small, we want to see it. For every person who either did someone a solid or wants to honor those who did, this is your moment. This is your contest. How To Participate We’re calling on the community to celebrate "Everyday Heroes" who make the 'verse a better place for us all. Show off your best screenshot that embodies heroism, grit, or selflessness, especially when helping out someone in need. Drake has always had your back, and now we want to honor those players who go the extra mile as well.  Some examples of the types of screenshots we are looking for: Reviving a teammate in a combat zone or providing another player with an escort through a dangerous route. Helping a friend move cargo or assisting someone with any task. Answering a rescue beacon or delivering much-needed supplies like food and drink. Refueling a stranded Citizen or providing a tow for a disabled ship. Please read the contest rules carefully to avoid disqualification. :camera_with_flash: Capture: Either snap a screenshot of an act of everyday heroism or recreate one you've experienced. If it made a difference to someone, it counts.  :outbox_tray: Submit: Post your entry to the Community Hub, using the DefenseCon announcement at the top of the Community Hub page. Multiple submissions are allowed throughout the event period, so feel free to experiment and try different ideas. Keep In Mind! Posts must be submitted to the Community Hub within the correct DefenseCon category. Each submission must clearly reflect an act of goodwill, selflessness, or perseverance that benefits someone in need. Post-processing effects are not allowed. AI-generated or AI-edited content is not allowed Replies to this thread will not count as submissions. Multiple players may appear in your screenshot, but group collaborations are not allowed. Only the submitting player is eligible to win. Multiple submissions are allowed. Winning Conditions The CIG jury will judge your submissions on the following: Visual quality Creativity and composition Strong interpretation of the “Everyday Heroes” theme Clear sense of an act of perseverance in the face of hardship, bravery, or helpfulness toward others Dates The submission period ends on Wednesday, May 27, 2026, 20:00 UTC. Rewards  A special thanks to our friends at Tobii for sponsoring two Eye Tracker 5 for this contest!   :first_place_medal: 1st Place: Tobii Eye Tracker 5, Origin M80 in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and Dynasty Paint :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: Tobii Eye Tracker 5, Drake Cutlass in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) & Drake Pitbull in-game ship with LTI and Windchill Paint :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: MISC Starlite in-game ship with LTI (in-game lifetime insurance) and Empyrean Paint & MISC Hull A in-game ship with LTI  It's a dangerous 'verse, but help is on the way. Winners  :first_place_medal: 1st Place: @XingKongCFR delivered the light of hope for a Citizen in need. // Entry  :second_place_medal: 2nd Place: @WhosButWhyTho is saving lives and taking names. // Entry   :third_place_medal: 3rd Place: @Reader_One patrols the skies to keep us safe. // Entry

title: Re: Billions of AUEC already being sold
summary: The claims around billions of aUEC circulating right now don’t line up with what we’re currently seeing internally. While I can’t get into specifics around monitoring or enforcement, our tools and visibility today are significantly more robust than they were previously, and we absolutely will take action and clean things up where needed. Since the economy is server-side, we have a pretty clear picture of the overall economy, and the highest balances we’re currently seeing are still only in the millions (not even 5% of a billion).  It’s also important to note that it’s pretty common for RMT sellers to attempt to sell currency they do not actually have, especially after an economy reset. Aside from being against the TOS, there’s also a pretty high likelihood of getting scammed.

title: Roadmap Roundup - May 20, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates. Space Combat Missions - Defend Location Adding missions where players are now defending a location from NPC Attackers. This includes a standalone mission and a compounding one where players will have multiple conflicting priorities to complete. :scroll: This card has been set to Committed.

title: Re: Will you say anything about Ironclad ?
summary: Hey there,  The teams have tracked, reproduced, and are currently working on multiple fixes for the Ironclad.  I can confirm that several of the top Ironclad Issue Council reports are actively being addressed, including: Ironclad switching from NAV mode to SCM mode → Fixed internally and ready for implementation Command Module separating from the Ironclad during quantum travel → Fixed internally and ready for implementation Suffocating inside the Ironclad → Actively under investigation. While we’ve fixed most of the door air gap issues, there are still a few missing atmosphere pockets in the Ironclad Assault caused by door geometry. We’re continuing to work on those fixes. We’re also aware of others issues involving for example the Ironclad radar, persistent quantum sound loops, random explosions while docked, third-person camera focus being locked to the Command Module, lights that cannot be turned off, or trespassing warnings. We truly appreciate all your reports on the Issue Council, they help the teams reproduce, investigate, and resolve these issues much faster.  Thanks again for your patience while we continue working on improvements.

summary: Hi folks,  Quick update on several issues we've been tracking. Many are in progress, but here are the freshest ones:   :white_check_mark: Hotfixed to Live recently Some ships could not be claimed through "Claim Insured Loadout" The mobiGlas Starmap "Route" button had an incorrect interaction area. In cases where the button itself was not responsive, the clickable area was shifted slightly to the right. You could still reliably use [R] to set routes. Docking issues preventing both manual and automatic docking at certain stations have also been hotfixed to Live.  :white_check_mark: Fixed (May 21, reminder) Purchased pledge items not appearing in-game should now be resolved with the new Individual Claim Mode: Freight elevators now include a new "Claim Mode" button at your home location. This allows you to reclaim platform-owned ship items such as paints and gear individually back to your home inventory. Previously owned instances of claimed items will be invalidated automatically. For easier navigation, there is also an "Exclude Paints" filter option available. If you are still missing pledged items after the update, please perform a Character Repair and let us know if the issue persists afterward. We continue to monitor this one.  :hammer_and_wrench: Reproduced and In Progress Scanning and targeting currently don't function correctly when the Command Module is docked to a host vehicle. Scanning is failing to return signatures for vehicles and objects in this state. The team has successfully reproduced the issue and work is ongoing.  :mag: Investigating We are actively investigating your reports regarding lost Personal Hangars. We know how disruptive this issue is and are currently investigating solutions, though it may not make the 4.8 release window. We'll keep you in the loop.  :hourglass_flowing_sand: Fixed, Awaiting Implementation An issue causing the Syulen interaction buttons to become difficult or impossible to press has been fixed two hours ago and is currently awaiting implementation into an upcoming build. Regarding duplication exploits, this remains an active area of focus for the teams. Several fixes have already gone out, and we greatly appreciate everyone continuing to report these issues through the Issue Council or directly to us. We are actively tracking and working on additional exploits fixes as well.  We'll have more news soon as we continue to hammer the issues you have been reporting recently.  Cheers,

title: Re: Star Citizen VR Support - Experimental Release (Alpha 4.8/4.9/4.10)
summary: Hello everyone! I’m happy to announce that 4.8.1 which is coming soon will fix the majority of remaining UI issues for VR. This includes marker, salvage and tractor overlays. This rework is only active in VR for now and there are a bunch of console variables which can be tuned for your liking with more to come in the future.  ui_markers.enabled_3d: Enables the new 3D world space marker system. When disabled, markers use the legacy 2D screen space positioning. This is already forced on in VR but can be used to enable the 3d markers in desktop mode too. Longterm the 2d version will be removed.  ui_markers.scale_3d: Adjusts the overall size of all 3D markers.  ui_markers.offscreen_distance_3d: Controls how far from the camera offscreen (edge) markers are placed in world space.  ui_markers.offscreen_angle_3d: Controls how close offscreen markers appear to the edge of the screen. Higher values place them closer to the field of view boundary.  ui_markers.bounds_offset_scale_3d: Adjusts the distance between markers and the tracked object. Increase this value to move labels further away from the object.  ui_markers.bounds_offset_angle_3d: Adds an angular offset to marker positioning at longer distances.  If you have any issues or suggestions please let me know!  What is still planned:  - Global variable to set opacity for markers - Change opacity of Markers on the backside of a planet  Fly safe o7 SilvanCIG

title: Roadmap Roundup - June 3, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team Alpha 4.8 Space Combat Missions - Defend Location Implementing a new Mission Pack for players to answer the call from either Foxwell or Headhunters. Defend asteroid bases throughout the systems, prevent the attackers from destroying key resources, and sometimes escort escaping workers to safety. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.   Alpha 4.9 Siege of Orison Implementing a new operation, Siege of Orison, introducing instanced FPS  gameplay where players assault Nine Tails-controlled platforms in  coordinated team-based encounters tied to mission-driven progression. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Instancing Implementing Instancing to create closed gameplay spaces with controlled accesses. Access is managed through instance prerequisites, party leader ownership, and safeguards that prevent or remove ineligible players. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Super Heavy Combat Armor Implementing the Super Heavy armor class, enabling players to equip and operate a new category of powerful super heavy weapons. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Apocalypse Arms "Vendetta" HMG Implementing a brand new weapon type: the Heavy Machine Gun, with the Apocalypse Arms "Vendetta" HMG. Belt-fed and usable with the new Super Heavy Armor and its dedicated ammunition backpack, it delivers sustained high-rate fire from a large rotating barrel while carrying up to four magazines of ammunition. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Combat Clothing Implementing lightly armored apparel designed to offer a more stylish look while remaining viable in combat situations. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  New Wikelo Ships Offerings (4.9.0) Adding a Drake Clipper with a unique base livery and upgraded components as a reward for completing a new addition to the variety of available Wikelo's Emporium contracts. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Mission Giver: Recco Battaglia Implementing a returning NPC to the Persistent Universe: Recco coordinates logistics for the local independent miners operating from Levski.  :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.

title: Star Citizen Alpha 4.8.1 LIVE - Hotfix 11952564
summary: Star Citizen Alpha Patch 4.8.1 LIVE Alpha Patch 4.8.1 has now been released onto the LIVE Environment with a new hotfix! Launcher should now show: VERSION 4.8.1-LIVE.11952564.  Important Build Info     Long Term Persistence: Enabled     Starting aUEC: 20,000  This Spectrum post is an abridged version of the notes. For the full in-depth details, please visit the main notes at the link below! Star Citizen Alpha 4.8 LIVE Release Notes   Feature Updates  Player Trade Notifications Refactor with Economy Authorization Service Replacing the player aUEC trade flow with an authorization-ticket model that will require both parties to consent to the trade before it completes. The receiving player will receive a notification alert when aUEC is sent, prompting them to accept or deny. The sender will have a pending message. If not accepted in time by the receiver, the transaction will cancel. This system also introduces trade rate limits and amount caps.  For further information on aUEC trades, head on over to the community post about this topic https://robertsspaceindustries.com/spectrum/community/SC/forum/3/thread/player-to-player-trade-update   Hangar Collision Insurance Update Players will now receive a free insurance claim when their ship is destroyed due to collision inside a hangar.   Experimental VR Updates: 3d UI Markers & Tractor AR Added new 3D Versions for all marker types which can be activated with CVAR "ui_markers.enabled_3d", i.e. Vehicle Entrance, Object Markers, POI Markers, proper 3D transformation to Jump point markers. Tractor and Structural AR: 2D version has been removed. Desktop also uses the new 3D version now.  IMPORTANT Notes: The 3D versions look slightly different but they are almost identical to the 2D version: New projection helpers have been added to calculate the proper AR RTT local space position and the projected distance which scales with FOV and distance so 3D elements have always the same size New Cvars: ui_markers.enabled_3d - Switches markers between legacy 2D screenspace positioning and the new 3D world-space transform system. ui_markers.scale_3d - Uniform size scale applied to all 3D markers. ui_markers.max_distance_3d - Clamps the render distance of 3D markers to avoid floating-point precision issues from Building Blocks 32-bit coordinate space. ui_markers.offscreen_distance_3d - World-space distance from the camera at which offscreen (edge) markers are placed. ui_markers.offscreen_angle_3d - How far from screen centre offscreen markers sit, in degrees. Higher values push them closer to the FOV edge. ui_markers.offscreen_pitch_offset_3d - Tilts the reference forward direction for offscreen markers; intended for VR comfort tuning. ui_markers.bounds_offset_scale_3d - Flat multiplier on the above/below offset used to position labels relative to the ship's bounds. Increase to push labels further away from the ship body. ui_markers.bounds_offset_angle_3d - Angular offset (degrees) added to the 3D bounds position at range. pl_visor_markerAR.hud_ar_projected_size_scale - Scales the entire UI by this factor which uses the projected size   Bugfixes & Technical Escort Ship missions are currently unavailable while we test fixes for blocking issues. Once the fixes are confirmed as resolved, the missions will re-appear in your Contracts Manager on LIVE. This update includes multiple client and server stability improvements and crash fixes.  This update also includes half a dozen exploit fixes. Due to the nature of these, they will not be listed.  We've completed further technical work to address the character repair causing a number of accounts to "brick" and have included that in today's hotfix. Potential Fix: Issue where the active route would reset when switching between SCM and NAV modes on ships equipped with the Command Module Potential Fix: Issue where vehicles would stop mid-flight or during Quantum Travel and the Command Module would undock on its own Potential Fix: The interaction prompt for the Cargo Module disappears after reclaiming insured vehicles with the Cargo Module equipped Potential Fix: Issue where Quantum Travel markers did not behave correctly when a route was set on an Ironclad or Caterpillar spawned with the Command Module attached Potential Fix: Issue where the "Route" button's clickable area did not match its visible UI element on the Starmap Potential Fix: Issue where players were unable to dock at spaceports using Docking Collars across multiple systems Potential Fix: Issue where the MISC Starfarer's external fuel tanks could be detached via the fuel console without first unlocking the vehicle item ports. Potential Fix: Issue where Meteor weapons could be swapped out for generic Size 5 weapons Potential Fix: Issue where the Aegis Tiburon pilot lost their targeting pips when another player entered a remote turret. Star Citizen Alpha 4.8 LIVE Release Notes Feature Updates Player Trade Notifications Refactor with Economy Authorization Service Replacing the player aUEC trade flow with an authorization-ticket model that will require both parties to consent to the trade before it completes. The receiving player will receive a notification alert when aUEC is sent, prompting them to accept or deny. The sender will have a pending message. If not accepted in time by the receiver, the transaction will cancel. This system also introduces trade rate limits and amount caps. For further information on aUEC trades, head on over to the community post about this topic https://robertsspaceindustries.com/spectrum/community/SC/forum/3/thread/player-to-player-trade-update Hangar Collision Insurance Update Players will now receive a free insurance claim when their ship is destroyed due to collision inside a hangar. Experimental VR Updates: 3d UI Markers & Tractor AR Added new 3D Versions for all marker types which can be activated with CVAR "ui_markers.enabled_3d", i.e. Vehicle Entrance, Object Markers, POI Markers, proper 3D transformation to Jump point markers. Tractor and Structural AR: 2D version has been removed. Desktop also uses the new 3D version now. IMPORTANT Notes: The 3D versions look slightly different but they are almost identical to the 2D version: New projection helpers have been added to calculate the proper AR RTT local space position and the projected distance which scales with FOV and distance so 3D elements have always the same size New Cvars: ui_markers.enabled_3d - Switches markers between legacy 2D screenspace positioning and the new 3D world-space transform system. ui_markers.scale_3d - Uniform size scale applied to all 3D markers. ui_markers.max_distance_3d - Clamps the render distance of 3D markers to avoid floating-point precision issues from Building Blocks 32-bit coordinate space. ui_markers.offscreen_distance_3d - World-space distance from the camera at which offscreen (edge) markers are placed. ui_markers.offscreen_angle_3d - How far from screen centre offscreen markers sit, in degrees. Higher values push them closer to the FOV edge. ui_markers.offscreen_pitch_offset_3d - Tilts the reference forward direction for offscreen markers; intended for VR comfort tuning. ui_markers.bounds_offset_scale_3d - Flat multiplier on the above/below offset used to position labels relative to the ship's bounds. Increase to push labels further away from the ship body. ui_markers.bounds_offset_angle_3d - Angular offset (degrees) added to the 3D bounds position at range. pl_visor_markerAR.hud_ar_projected_size_scale - Scales the entire UI by this factor which uses the projected size Bugfixes & Technical Escort Ship missions are currently unavailable while we test fixes for blocking issues. Once the fixes are confirmed as resolved, the missions will re-appear in your Contracts Manager on LIVE. This update includes multiple client and server stability improvements and crash fixes. This update also includes half a dozen exploit fixes. Due to the nature of these, they will not be listed. We've completed further technical work to address the character repair causing a number of accounts to "brick" and have included that in today's hotfix. title: Player-to-Player Trade Update
summary: Hi everyone,  With the latest 4.8 update, we've made some changes to how player-to-player transactions work. We wanted to give you a heads-up on what's changing, and be upfront that this is an area we'll be actively adjusting over the coming days and weeks.    What's New Trades between players now require both parties to be online, with the recipient acknowledging the transaction before it completes. This helps ensure transfers are intentional and confirmed on both ends.  The online requirement is a temporary step. In the future, we plan to support offline notification resolution, which will let you send a trade offer to a player who's offline while still preserving the acknowledgment flow. Until that's in place, both players will need to be online to complete a trade.  In addition, the UEE Bank now performs authorization verification on transactions, including limits on transaction rates and amounts.    Our Approach to Limits Our goal is to keep trade frictionless for players going about their normal business, while giving us the tools to identify and restrict abuse. We're working toward a flexible system of limits with multiple tiers, so that legitimate activity sits comfortably within them while unusual patterns can be flagged without affecting everyone else.  We don't expect to land on the right values straight away. Finding the balance will take some tuning, and we'll be adjusting as we learn more from real activity in the 'verse.    What to Expect Over the next few days and weeks, you may notice changes to rate limiting and transaction thresholds as we calibrate things. Some limits may feel conservative at first while we gather data and find the right settings. If something feels off, that feedback is genuinely useful to us during this period.   Thanks for bearing with us as we tune these systems. We appreciate your patience while we get this right.

title: Alpha 4.8.1 Known Issues Update
summary: Hey everyone,  We’ve seen a lot of reports and feedback come in since the release of Alpha 4.8.1, and the teams are working hard to address the issues you’ve been raising.  Before diving into the list, we want to acknowledge that some of these issues are having a significant impact on your game experience. Our teams have been spending a great deal of time investigating reports, reviewing logs, reproducing issues internally, and deploying fixes where possible. While some issues can be resolved quickly, generally through a hotfix, others require additional investigation to fully understand and address. We wanted to share where things currently stand on some of the most visible reports. Please note that the list is not exhaustive.   :scroll: Currently Investigating The following issues are actively being investigated, tested, or reviewed by the team: Inventory becoming unavailable, with backpack, station, and loot inventories appearing empty or inaccessible. We've identified a likely cause and are continuing to work through it with the goal of getting a fix in place as soon as we can. We've seen the reports around docking issues and are actively working to reproduce and isolate the causes behind them. Mined ores disappearing after storing a vehicle. Current investigation points toward resource container values reverting to a previously serialized state after stow/unstow. QV Warehouse loot not respawning or resetting correctly if cargo is looted without progressing through the mission, preventing subsequent players from accessing intended rewards. The team is actively testing potential fixes and reviewing the mission flow. Ironclad oxygen issues affecting multiple rooms: Resolved for most locations, with a small number of remaining reports still under investigation. A more comprehensive solution is planned for an upcoming update. Crafted item stats not always appearing in item descriptions while inside inventory spaces, making it difficult to verify item properties after crafting. Refueling notifications and Helpful Hints can become stuck and prevent notifications, party invites, mission shares, and other UI prompts from appearing correctly. The following workaround could help you out while we're working on a solution: Enable Helpful Hints and Keybind Hints in the Game Settings, close the menu, reopen it, then disable both options again and close the menu. Notifications should begin functioning normally again, though previously queued notifications may still appear afterward. Shard lock issues preventing some players from joining or remaining connected to sessions. This remains one of our high-priority investigations. We've already identified and addressed several contributing issues, and the team is continuing to work through additional fixes. Drake Command Module playing Quantum Travel spooling audio when spawned or streamed while attached to a host vehicle. This issue is known and under review for a future update.   :hourglass: Pending Implementation Potential fixes pending implementation to the Live version, fixed internally: Fuel nozzles on ships cannot be detached and swapped. Starfarer refuel exchange displaying incorrect values between microSCU and SCU. Players can asphyxiate inside the Drake Command Module despite having a helmet equipped. Pressure and temperature levels can spike drastically during navigation in the Drake Command Module due to atmosphere-related issues. Players can experience high pressure levels in certain areas of the Ironclad after undocking and re-docking the Command Module. Ironclad tractor beam range of motion and camera controls have been improved for better usability and cargo handling. ROC, ROC-DS, and Prospector mining heads now align more accurately with the mining reticle, improving mining precision. Visual issues affecting Banu Defender and Aopoa Khartu-Al paints have been resolved. Players can once again exit the Argo MPUV Tractor pilot seat reliably using standard exit controls. The MIRAI Guardian radar display orientation has been corrected. Material issues affecting the front hull of the MISC Prospector have been fixed. Material issues affecting the Stinger canopy and HUD have been fixed, reducing excessive visual artifacts from rain and wear effects. F7 Mk I turret weapons now persist correctly and can once again be swapped as intended.   :white_check_mark: Fixed The following issues have been fixed in the current Live version: Drake Command Module unexpectedly undocking during Quantum Travel or general flight. Fixed in 4.8 11904230. Aegis Tiburon tracking pips jittering out of position. Fixed in 4.8 11930495. Syulen interaction buttons being difficult or impossible to use. Fixed in 4.8 11940252. And more recent fixes in 4.8.1 LIVE - Hotfix 11952564.   :eye: Additional Reports We're Tracking The teams are also working hard on the following issues: Freight Elevators becoming stuck in personal hangars and blocking cargo access. Freight Elevators becoming stuck at outposts, preventing hauling missions from being completed. Missing Quantum Markers impacting navigation to destinations across the PU. Missing Jump Point markers after transiting in the Ironclad. Ironclad atmosphere inconsistencies affecting environmental conditions aboard the ship. Extremely low interior temperatures being reported inside certain ships. Command Module radar displays failing to appear in some situations. Moving an undersuit into inventory causing equipment functionality issues.   We'll continue to share updates through our Patch Notes threads and on Spectrum. For known issues and available workarounds, the Known Issues thread remains a great resource and is regularly updated as new information becomes available.  We'll also continue to keep you informed through the Status Page whenever degraded performance is detected. This doesn't necessarily mean a server outage has occurred, but rather that we're investigating elevated error rates or other service disruptions that may be impacting the experience.  As always, thank you for your reports, especially on the Issue Council, as it plays a crucial role in helping us identify, investigate, and resolve issues.

QV Warehouse loot not respawning or resetting correctly if cargo is looted without progressing through the mission, preventing subsequent players from accessing intended rewards. The team is actively testing potential fixes and reviewing the mission flow. Ironclad oxygen issues affecting multiple rooms: Resolved for most locations, with a small number of remaining reports still under investigation. A more comprehensive solution is planned for an upcoming update. Crafted item stats not always appearing in item descriptions while inside inventory spaces, making it difficult to verify item properties after crafting. Refueling notifications and Helpful Hints can become stuck and prevent notifications, party invites, mission shares, and other UI prompts from appearing correctly. The following workaround could help you out while we're working on a solution: Enable Helpful Hints and Keybind Hints in the Game Settings, close the menu, reopen it, then disable both options again and close the menu. Notifications should begin functioning normally again, though previously queued notifications may still appear afterward. Shard lock issues preventing some players from joining or remaining connected to sessions. This remains one of our high-priority investigations. We've already identified and addressed several contributing issues, and the team is continuing to work through additional fixes. Drake Command Module playing Quantum Travel spooling audio when spawned or streamed while attached to a host vehicle. This issue is known and under review for a future update. :hourglass: Pending Implementation Potential fixes pending implementation to the Live version, fixed internally: Fuel nozzles on ships cannot be detached and swapped. Starfarer refuel exchange displaying incorrect values between microSCU and SCU. Players can asphyxiate inside the Drake Command Module despite having a helmet equipped. Pressure and temperature levels can spike drastically during navigation in the Drake Command Module due to atmosphere-related issues. Players can experience high pressure levels in certain areas of the Ironclad after undocking and re-docking the Command Module. Ironclad tractor beam range of motion and camera controls have been improved for better usability and cargo handling. ROC, ROC-DS, and Prospector mining heads now align more accurately with the mining reticle, improving mining precision. Visual issues affecting Banu Defender and Aopoa Khartu-Al paints have been resolved. Players can once again exit the Argo MPUV Tractor pilot seat reliably using standard exit controls. The MIRAI Guardian radar display orientation has been corrected. Material issues affecting the front hull of the MISC Prospector have been fixed. Material issues affecting the Stinger canopy and HUD have been fixed, reducing excessive visual artifacts from rain and wear effects. F7 Mk I turret weapons now persist correctly and can once again be swapped as intended. :white_check_mark: Fixed The following issues have been fixed in the current Live version: Drake Command Module unexpectedly undocking during Quantum Travel or general flight. Fixed in 4.8 11904230. Aegis Tiburon tracking pips jittering out of position. Fixed in 4.8 11930495. Syulen interaction buttons being difficult or impossible to use. Fixed in 4.8 11940252. And more recent fixes in 4.8.1 LIVE - Hotfix 11952564. :eye: Additional Reports We're Tracking The teams are also working hard on the following issues: Freight Elevators becoming stuck in personal hangars and blocking cargo access. Freight Elevators becoming stuck at outposts, preventing hauling missions from being completed. Missing Quantum Markers impacting navigation to destinations across the PU. Missing Jump Point markers after transiting in the Ironclad. Ironclad atmosphere inconsistencies affecting environmental conditions aboard the ship. Extremely low interior temperatures being reported inside certain ships. Command Module radar displays failing to appear in some situations. Moving an undersuit into inventory causing equipment functionality issues. We'll continue to share updates through our Patch Notes threads and on Spectrum. For known issues and available workarounds, the Known Issues thread remains a great resource and is regularly updated as new information becomes available. We'll also continue to keep you informed through the Status Page whenever degraded performance is detected. This doesn't necessarily mean a server outage has occurred, but rather that we're investigating elevated error rates or other service disruptions that may be impacting the experience. As always, thank you for your reports, especially on the Issue Council, as it plays a crucial role in helping us identify, investigate, and resolve issues.

title: Roadmap Roundup - June 17, 2026
summary: Hello everyone!  Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible.  The 1.0 column showcases features and content planned for inclusion in or before Star Citizen 1.0. This means you may not have to wait for the 1.0 release to experience them. As features/content in the 1.0 column become ready, they will migrate left into a point patch column for release.  Be sure to check back every two weeks for the latest updates.  With that, let’s dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!  -CIG Community Team Alpha 4.8 Gatac Railen Implementing the Gatac Railen. Human-operable yet distinctly alien, the Railen bursts into long-haul transport with agility, vertical design, and remarkable grav-lev employment. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.  Gatac Tyilui Implementing the Gatac Tyilui, the first alien-designed carrier on the market, and also the first ship with a zero-gravity hangar, allowing for an aerial ballet of weightless operation. :scroll: This card has been set to Released.   Alpha 4.9 Item Recovery: Ship Loadout Improvements Implementing Item Recovery: Ship Loadout Improvements, updating ship and item recovery to better support custom loadouts through timed claims, optional expedite fees, freight elevator item claims, and debuting a free recovery option when losses are detected as outside the player’s control. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Nine Tails Armor Update Implementing updated armor sets for the Nine Tails criminal organization, refreshing the appearance of grunts, elites, and boss NPCs. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Behring "CQ7" Bullpup Rifle Implementing the Behring "CQ7" Bullpup Rifle, a battle rifle purpose-built for close-quarters engagements, combining the compact handling of a bullpup design with the firepower needed for intense frontline and boarding combat. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  Ordnance Cargo Holder Implementing dedicated storage frames for missiles, torpedoes, and bombs placed on cargo grids to improve presentation and handling. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.  New Hairstyles (4.9.0) Implementing two new hairstyles, along with an update to one hairstyle to bring it up to current quality standards. :scroll: This card has been set to Tentative.

title: [EVO NDA] Star Citizen Alpha 4.9 PTU Patch Notes 12098675
summary: Star Citizen Alpha Patch 4.9  Alpha Patch 4.9 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 4.9.0-PTU.12098675. Audience: Evocati (Standard Evo NDA) Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only Long Term Persistence: Enabled  Testing/Feedback Focus Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases Instanced Siege of Orison (Will be focusing on the 1st Island in today's build) New Story Missions: Recco Battaglia Warning: There are going to be lots of content items in partial states of finished. Currently all balance and features are WIP  Known Issues PU - Ship Battles - Missions / Locations - Escort - Hangar doors are not opening for the ship that needs to be escorted Front End - Main Menu - Social / Add Friends - UI - Clicking add friends whilst in the main menu will make your UI uninteractable PU - Ship Battles V2 - EscortShips - Mission Content / AI - Escorted ship does not Quantum Travel away or Go to the Hangar after neutralizing the AI ships in the mission location PU - Missions - Bounty Hunter / Mission Content - When killing the Neutralize target the mission does not progress PU - Stanton - Siege of Orison V2 - Instancing / Mission / Locations - Server Error Causes Platforms to Despawn at SoO With this issue, if a server error does happen, you will need to leave and create a new instance, potentially reforming the party with a new leader. PU - Stanton - SOOV2 - Transport / Mission Content - Shuttle from Solanki to Hartmoore has no collision  PU - Stanton - Siege of Orison - Locations - Rooftop balcony cannot be accessed by players naturally on Solanki Platform  Because of these issues, we will only be focusing on the first island of Siege of Orison tonight Multi-System - PU - Locations / Inventory - There's a chance that their primary residence does not contain their items' Workaround: Recopy account if you need your default local items   Features & Gameplay Gameplay Instanced Siege of Orison Siege of Orison returns as a fully reworked, instanced co-operative FPS mission. This update introduces Mission Instancing to Star Citizen for the first time, a system that creates a private, closed environment shared only by you and your party.   This new version of Siege of Orison removes ship combat entirely and redesigns the experience as a focused, three-island FPS mission set in the Inspiration Park cluster. Ninetails have locked down access to the islands, overriding local security systems and stationing their lieutenants and the commander throughout the platforms. Crusader Security has contracted InterSec to get control back. Your objective on each island is the same: clear through the Ninetails resistance, reset the Security Network Control Towers, defeat the island Lieutenant, and flip the IFFI to restore Crusader's airspace control then move to the next island.  Each island is progressively more difficult, with the final island culminating in a boss fight against Mendo Ren inside the Admin Center barge. Level design across all three islands has been updated for better sightlines, improved combat flow, and navigation that suits the instanced, no-ship format. Tonight's test will focus highly on the 1st island.     // Instancing & Siege of Orison Closed Instance - Max 4 Players When you enter the instance elevator, it locks to you and your party. No other players can join without being invited. The maximum party size for this instance is four. If you try to enter as a group of six, the first four are admitted and the remaining two are notified they cannot enter. Entering & Mission Acceptance An optional one-time Intro Contract is available anywhere in Stanton that directs first-time players to the instance entrance at the Crusader Showroom Rooftop. On any subsequent visit, you can enter directly. When you step into the instance, the Siege of Orison mission is automatically accepted for everyone in the party with no manual pickup required. Entering Solo You can enter the instance alone and play solo, or share the auto-accepted mission with other players to allow them to join your instance after you are inside. Entrance Location Take the elevator to the Crusader Showroom Rooftop in Orison. From there, board the shuttle to the Instance Transit Platform and enter the instance via the elevator on the platform. The transit platform serves as a staging area between islands throughout the mission.   New Mission Giver: Recco Battaglia In tonight's build, we will have the new narrative story missions from Recco Battaglia available. You'll get to play all three chapters for which the first one is available from by default, though Chapters 2 and 3 are available once you've gained enough reputation by completing other repeatable contracts Battaglia is offering. To ensure you get to experience all of these missions in a reasonable timeframe, we've lowered the reputation requirements for the later missions. You will be able to see and accept these missions in the mobiGlas while in Nyx. Players will see distinct markers to indicate whether a shot hit shields, impacted the hull, penetrated armor, destroyed an internal component, or was deflected entirely. title: [Wave 1] Star Citizen Alpha 4.9 PTU Patch Notes 12118066
summary: Star Citizen Alpha Patch 4.9 Alpha Patch 4.9 has been released and is now available to test on the PTU environment! Patch should now show: VERSION 4.9.0-PTU.12118066         Audience: Wave 1         Server Info: PTU Channel - US Only         Long Term Persistence: Enabled Testing/Feedback Focus         Stability, Bugfixes, LTP between PTU releases         Recco Battaglia Repeatable Missions (story missions disabled in tonight's build)     Vehicle Hit Marker Updates  Known Issues        Destroy Narcotics missions disabled temporarily due to a structural refactor      PU - Ship Battles - Missions / Locations - Escort - Hangar doors are not opening for the ship that needs to be escorted         PU - Ship Battles V2 - EscortShips - Mission Content / AI - Escorted ship does not Quantum Travel away or Go to the Hangar after neutralizing the AI ships in the mission location         PU - Missions - Bounty Hunter / Mission Content - When killing the Neutralize target the mission does not progress Front End - Socials / Add Friends - UI / Online Services - Searching for friends on the Add Friends search bar will result in a "Service Unavailable" PU - Commodity Kiosks - Multiple Locations - "Failed" error appears when buying RMC from Commodity Kiosks         Multi-System - PU - Locations / Inventory - There's a chance that their primary residence does not contain their items' Workaround: Recopy account if you need your default local items   Features & Gameplay     Gameplay Missile Cargo Grid Visuals & Ship Servicing Improvements Missiles/Torpedoes placed on a cargo grid will now display a bounding box frame around them, giving a clearer visual reference for the space each missile occupies. This frame is visible anywhere a cargo grid is present, including ship interiors and freight elevators. When snapping a missile into position, both the missile and its frame are now shown in the hologram preview, and players can choose the snapping direction during placement.
